description.narrative: Supports the following illustrative program-funded costs: salaries of US, FSN, and TCN and other staff such as PSCs, RSSAs, PASAs, CASUs working for the US Government managing, administering, and supporting programs and their program-funded benefits such as housing, travel, transportation, education allowances etc; institutional contractors that provide such staff, rent, IT services, the program-funded share of utilities, staff training costs and the cost of developing and administering training programs, equipment and supplies, ICASS, vehicle fuel and maintenance, maintenance contracts, janitorial services, operational unit web page development and maintenance, outreach such as publications and the cost of their preparation (including staff costs), and technical assistance to ensure USG compliance with regulations.

HIV/AIDS - Improve the lives of orphans and other vulnerable children and families affected by HIV/AIDS. Strengthen communities to meet the needs of orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, supporting community-based responses, helping children and adolescents to meet their own needs, creating a supportive social and policy environment. Activities could include training caregivers, increasing access to education, economic support, targeted food and nutrition support, and legal aid. Institutional responses would also be included. ARV treatment of children is excluded from this category and should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and Sub-Element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). Palliative care, including basic health care and support and TB/HIV prevention, management and treatment, as well as their related laboratory services and pharmaceuticals, when delivered within programs for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under this aspect. Other health care associated with the continuum of HIV/AIDS illness, including HIV/TB services, when delivered outside a program for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.6 (Basic Health Care and Support) or Sub-Element 1.1.7 (TB/HIV).

description.narrative: Promote sustainable improvements in health outcomes by reducing key health systems constraints to achieve the goals and objectives of multiple health elements and the health area overall. Activities coded here aim to promote financial protection, efficiency, and affordability of health services in general; ensure the quality or availability of an essential package of prevention, promotion, treatment and care services; enhance equitable access to priority services by under-served, marginalized and other high priority groups; and ensure responsiveness to people's expectations. Such activities strengthen the core health systems functions/building blocks (leadership and governance; finance; human resources for health; medicines, vaccines and technology; and service delivery). Note 1: Operating Units should report activities that address specific element goals under other elements, reserving the use of this cross-cutting health systems strengthening element for overarching activities that are supported with multiple health element funding. Note 2: Operating units should report activities that strengthen the information function of the health system under the Host Country Strategic Information Systems element.

description.narrative: Lewa -- Northern Rangeland Trust Program

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Legislative Function and Processes - Legislative Strengthening and Legal Reform

description.narrative: Improve the way the legislature and legislative processes and procedures work to uphold democratic practices. Focus on the quality and effectiveness of legislation, including the constitution, codes, laws, and regulations applying to various development sectors. Increase the legislatures capacity to be responsive to the people it serves, enhance public participation, engage in policy-making, hold itself and the executive accountable, and oversee the implementation of government programs, budgets, and laws.

Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). Build the capacity of civil society organizations to act as agents for reform and support their participation in democratic decision-making through articulating and representing their members interests, engaging in service delivery, and advocating for issues which become part of the public agenda and are reflected in public policies. Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.

title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Host Country Strategic Information Capacity (HIV)

description.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Improve the lives of orphans and other vulnerable children and families affected by HIV/AIDS. Strengthen communities to meet the needs of orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, supporting community-based responses, helping children and adolescents to meet their own needs, creating a supportive social and policy environment. Activities could include training caregivers, increasing access to education, economic support, targeted food and nutrition support, and legal aid. Institutional responses would also be included. ARV treatment of children is excluded from this category and should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and Sub-Element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). Palliative care, including basic health care and support and TB/HIV prevention, management and treatment, as well as their related laboratory services and pharmaceuticals, when delivered within programs for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under this aspect. Other health care associated with the continuum of HIV/AIDS illness, including HIV/TB services, when delivered outside a program for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.6 (Basic Health Care and Support) or Sub-Element 1.1.7 (TB/HIV).

title.narrative: KEMSA Fixed Amount Reimbursement Agreement (FARA) Implementation Letters

description.narrative: Kenya Medical Supplies Agency (KEMSA) is a customer-focused integrated medical logistics provider for all public health facilities in Kenya. As a State Corporation, KEMSA is a secure source of value-for-money drugs and other medical supplies to over 5,000 facilities. KEMSA has also received substantial TA and support from USAID in human resource capacity building through the deployment of key advisors in areas of business development, procurement, IT and supply chain management. With USAID support, KEMSA has invested in an effective Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system that has led to the full automation and integration of KEMSA operations and overall business processes, resulting in greater efficiency and improved service delivery. KEMSA's fully automated central warehouse in Nairobi is now functioning under the platform of a Warehouse Module System hosted by the ERP. This has significantly improved efficiency in inventory management and processing of health facilities requirements. KEMSA has successfully implemented the Framework Contract system, and all current procurements are aligned to KEMSAs strategic and business plan with enhanced visibility of all health care commodities in the supply chain. Currently KEMSA has a total allocation of KES 5.3 Billion ($60m) for essential medical supplies, approximately KES7.0 billion ($85m) for programs such as HIV, malaria and tuberculosis. KEMSA has been appointed as the procurement agent for the GFATM R10 procurements, and the USG is confident that KEMSA is re.ady to start handling some PEPFAR commodities. This is a new award, and no vehicle procurement is planned. This activity supports GHI/LLC and is funded primarily with pipeline funds in this budget cycle.

description.narrative: The USAID-funded Kenya Horticulture Development Project is a five-year 'Feed the Future' initiative funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and implemented by Fintrac, a leading US Agribusiness consulting company. USAID -KHCP is designed to achieve catalytic change leading to enhanced food security, increased incomes, and gender and youth equity in the horticultural sector. USAID-KHCP, in close collaboration with public and private sector organizations, employs a holistic approach to increasing competitiveness by delivering tailored assistance to entrepreneurial smallholder farmers with the aim to: 1) Enhance productivity and food security; 2) Increase value - addition; 3) Improving value - chain coordination, marketing, and trade promotion; 4) Improve business environment and institutional capacity.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

title.narrative: HIV Service Delivery Support Activity (HSDSA) Cluster 3

description.narrative: The overall goal of this activity is to increase access and coverage for HIV prevention, care and treatment services towards achieving the "90-90-90" targets. The following objectives of the activity are: 1. Increased availability and use of combination prevention services; 2. Increased uptake of targeted HIV testing services; 3. Improved linkage to treatment for individuals newly testing positive for HIV; 4. Increased uptake of and adherence to quality HIV treatment services; 5. Long-term follow up of patients receiving care and treatment services including laboratory and logistics support; and 6. Strengthened institutional accountability for the management of community, facility and county HIV response.

title.narrative: Tupime Kaunti - County Measurements, Learning and Accountability Program (CMLAP) II

description.narrative: Tupime Kaunti is a five-year USAID-funded project that contributes to Kenya Health Sector Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Frameworks goal of one functional, sector-wide M&E system for improved decision-making, transparency, and accountability in health. The project works with county governments to strengthen outcome MLA systems to provide quality data and synthesized information for planning, implementation, policy development and decision making. Tupime Kaunti works in nine counties including Kakamega, Kisumu, Kisii, Migori, Busia, Bungoma, Vihiga, Homa Bay and Siaya. The project focuses its support in HIV, malaria and RMNCAH programs. The project is implemented by a consortium of Palladium Group (lead), Kenya School of Government and Plan International.

title.narrative: ENV - Combating Wildlife Crime in Kenya Program

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2021 funding, USAID will continue to support the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) and the Ministry of Tourism and Wildlife to scale up their ability to combat wildlife trafficking activities. The award seeks to: i) improve organizational capacity and support policy reforms; ii) maintain connectivity and improve ecosystem integrity and resilience; iii) enhance partnership, community engagement and improve Wildlife Protection & Security; and vi) secure conservation financing by diversification of wildlife and tourism enterprises. The project supports Kenya's sustainability efforts by aligning and informing relevant deliverables under the new National Wildlife Conservation and Management Strategy which KWS is responsible for implementing. The KWS five-year Strategic Plan (2019- 2024) includes: the Implementation Letter -IL No. ENV-MoTW-1with the Ministry of Tourism and Wildlife for Projects and Activities under USAID Grant Agreement No. 615-DOAG-KEN-20-00, priority listing the 2018 KWS Organizational Risk Assessment Report.The program also supports several U.S. government priorities, including the USAID Biodiversity Policy, the U.S. National Strategy for Combating Wildlife Trafficking, the Eliminate, Neutralize and Disrupt (END) Wildlife Trafficking Act and USAID's Gender Equality and Women Empowerment (GEWE) Policy. The conservation and management of wildlife and landscapes is a key element of nature based solutions for climate mitigation. Through the implementation of this activity, it will advance the U.S. Foreign Policy and National Security on tackling the climate crisis. $800,000 and $100,000 of funding within this IM contributes to meeting the required "combating wildlife trafficking" of $3,800,000 and adaptation indirect of $1,300,000 earmarks.

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2022 resources, will support the Kenya Tuberculosis Accelerated Response and Care II (TB-ARC II) activity to provide support at the national and county levels to reduce tuberculosis (TB) incidence and deaths. Major interventions under the activity will include supporting improvements in the quality of existing TB diagnostic and treatment networks, strengthening services to accommodate a larger number of patients, and increasing case identification of TB, TB/HIV, and Drug Resistant-TB, including amongst children. The activity will enhance the efficiency and sustainability of the Kenya National Tuberculosis Program by building on the existing national treatment platforms and working to further increase the timely use of quality TB treatment services. The activity contributes to the attainment of U.S. Embassy Nairobi's Integrated Country Strategy Goal 3 of promoting a healthy, educated and productive Kenyan population to drive inclusive and sustainable development in the health sector. The activity will also provide technical assistance for local adaptation and scale-up of globally proven interventions, and will strengthen monitoring and evaluation of TB, and TB/HIV control interventions. Infectious disease prevention, detection and response is a priority U.S. security concerns as such diseases could spread beyond Kenya's borders. This activity also closely works with Kenyan TB experts, building their respective capacities and commitment to better plan and implement Kenya-led TB programs. This activity is also receiving HIV funds $1,022,001 in COP22..

title.narrative: DGC- Safeguarding Democratic Space in Kenya (SADES-K)

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Peaceful coexistence within a rule of law, accountable.government, and adequate data to drive decision-making and inform advocacy are.fundamental components of a flourishing democracy, yet much of these are still.lacking in Kenya. SADES-K promotes social and ethnic cohesion and supports.civil society advocacy to expand civic space (including press freedom). It also.aims to ensure governance reforms and reconciliation processes through the.Building Bridges to National Unity Initiative (BBI) is inclusive and responsive.to citizens. Through local Civil Society Organization (CSO) grants, the program.will educate and support citizens to advocate for a stronger civil society role.in advancing matters of public interest. To address pervasive corruption and.abuse of office, SADES-K will issue a grant to a consortium of CSOs to work.with religious and anti-corruption networks to galvanize a citizen's movement.and campaign against corruption. In partnership with the University of Nairobi,.SADES-K will support regular public opinion research and political economy.analyses on themes such as corruption, elections, land, and devolution to.identify motivations, interests, movers and shakers, as well as unwritten rules.that promote or block key reforms.These reports will be used to develop and.implement advocacy strategies by key actors in the national conversation and.dialogue process to ensure accountability for commitments made by Kenya's.political leadership to the Kenyan people. The program supports the United.States Bilateral Strategic Dialogue priorities for good governance and civilian.security that seeks to deepen democratic reforms while strengthening the rule.of law, human rights, and civic space. It strengthens Kenya's capacity and.commitment to accountable governance, a key milestone on the Journey to Self-Reliance...

description.narrative: Expand sustainable provision of FP/RH service in clinical and non-clinical programs including those in the public, private, NGO and PVO sectors, and at the community level; activities that help improve the quality of the services and care provided including pre- and in-service training of providers and application of evidence-based service delivery norms and standards; and availability of a wide range of contraceptive options (temporary methods, fertility awareness methods, long-acting reversible and permanent methods) for men and women. (N.B. Commodity procurement/ supply chain assistance is HL.7.6, a separate element.) Improve responsiveness to client needs including the FP/RH needs of youth and men, women and girls affected by violence, refugees/IDP, and other underserved populations. Included are activities that integrate FP and related RH care, including integrated FP/MCH services, especially provision of postpartum FP, FP information within the ANC setting, and post-abortion care; FP in the context of HIV/AIDS/STI prevention, treatment, care and support; fistula prevention and repair; prevention and mitigation of gender-based violence in the context of FP/RH programs; and programs that encourage abandonment of female genital cutting and other harmful traditional practices associated with negative RH outcomes. Facility construction and renovation specifically for FP/RH service delivery improvements is also included in this element.

title.narrative: HPN - Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops(KCCB) - Komesha TB program

description.narrative: (Kenya): USAID will utilize FY 2022 funds to invest in the Komesha Tuberculosis activity which provides county level support for the faith-based sector to reduce tuberculosis (TB) incidence and deaths. The activity will identify and empower community actors, stakeholders and TB champions to screen and refer presumptive TB cases to health facilities and will utilize faith-based media outlets and dialogue platforms to promote adherence to TB related services. The activity will collaborate with county health management teams to strengthen the capacity of faith-based health facilities to provide TB prevention, diagnosis, care and treatment services. The activity works with the National TB Programme and county teams and engages a variety of public and non-public stakeholders in development of annual county/sub-county TB work plans. The activity also expands GeneXpert networking through sensitization, specimen referral and external quality assurance to promptly identify new TB patients and place them immediately on TB treatment, hence reducing TB mortalities. Infectious disease prevention, detection and response is a priority for the U.S. security concerns as such diseases would otherwise spread beyond Kenya's borders. .

title.narrative: HPN - Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS) USAID Supply Chain Strengthening (KEMSA follow on)

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Using FY 2022 funds, USAID will support the Supply Chain Strengthening activity to warehouse and distribute health commodities funded by the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and President's Malaria Initiative (PMI). The activity will be implemented by the Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS), a Christian not-for-profit organization whose functions include the warehousing and distribution of medications and medical supplies. Under this activity, MEDS will manage warehousing and distribution for PEPFAR commodities and PMI-procured malaria rapid diagnostic tests, malaria medicines and insecticide-treated nets from the central warehouse to public sector health facilities nationwide. USAID will also support through this activity the procurement, warehousing and distribution of vayu - bCPAP machines to health facilities providing maternal and newborn care in USAID counties. The vayu - bCPAP machine is an evidence based life saving solution to addressing newborn deaths caused by prematurity and low birth weight. This intervention, complemented by other health system strengthening strategies, will contribute to the reduction of neonatal mortality to fewer than 10 per 1000 live births per the targets established in the Every Newborn Action Plan (ENP)..Generally speaking, USAID investments in MEDS will strengthen local health sector capacity to manage complex supply chain systems. This serves to build more stable and capable local systems which in turn boosts U.S national security objectives and improves public opinions of the United States in Kenya, as well as asserting U.S. influence and leadership in global health..

title.narrative: HPN - Cluster 6: FP/RMNCAH and Nutrition in Turkana

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2022 funds, USAID will support the Imarisha Jamii activity to increase the use of quality county-led health services in Turkana County through a service delivery systems approach. The county is currently intensely affected by one the worst droughts experienced in the region in 40 years and is in dire need of humanitarian assistance in addition to outreach focused and integrated health services to meet the needs of the mobile pastoralist populations as they search for food and pasture for what is left of their animals.The activity will utilize innovative context-specific strategies to increase the knowledge of and demand for essential services and multi-sectoral approaches to achieve results within an integrated activity. USAID investments will strengthen health systems and build local capacity and resilience for maternal, adolescent,newborn, child health and nutrition (RMNCAH) and nutrition. Specifically, the activity will strengthen health systems by:Building the capacity of county and sub-county health managers on leadership, management, accountability and governance.Creating awareness within counties on domestic resource mobilization approaches and ring fencing of health budgets, so as to increase and secure health related budgets.Improving access to antenatal care and skilled birth attendance through advancing universal health coverage by increasing the number of health facilities enrolled in Linda Mama/Free Maternity Services rolled out by the National Health Insurance Fund among rural populations.Improving health information systems to provide quality and timely data in District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2).Supporting counties in building strong integrated commodity supply systems at facility, sub- county and county levels..$200,000 of the $1,000,000 will be used to meet the "micronutrients" earmark under this activity..

(Kenya): .USAID will utilize FY 2022 funds to implement the Afya Uwazi activity which is a third-party monitoring (TPM) activity that seeks to establish a comprehensive commodity surveillance system that will provide USAID, the Government of Kenya, and Kenyan counties with a unified platform and a set of tools for monitoring, analyzing and visualizing supply chain performance and risk by county, facility and commodity. In recent years, the Kenya public health supply chain, managed through the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority (KEMSA), has faced challenges related to visibility and inventory management and struggled to demonstrate sustained improvements in performance, accountability and transparency. This independent third-party surveillance system supports an end-to-end visibility of health commodities as they move through the supply chain. ..The activity will maintain a commodity surveillance system informed by the risk control framework and strategic engagement with key stakeholders. The activity will also be complemented by collaboration and networking with other supply chain and service delivery implementing partners to improve supply chain transparency and accountability. The activity reinforces the Mission's priority on zero tolerance to health commodity losses and the need to shift responsibility for monitoring and improving the supply chain to individual counties...

The project also focuses on building the capacity of the umbrella organization, LCA, which is a locally owned organization in this important landscape. By building collaboration among conservancies and with other stakeholders, natural resource management will improve and help alleviate natural resources as a driver of conflict in northern Kenya.

description.narrative: Audit Services

(Kenya): Using FY 2022 funds, USAID will continue its support for the Western Kenya Sanitation Activity that is working to develop a robust sanitation and hygiene market to enable the adoption of higher quality latrines and county-wide access to hygiene products. The activity develops and reinforces market-based solutions, partnerships and learning interventions which address systemic barriers to improved sanitation, hygiene and menstrual health hygiene.The county-wide approach of strengthening markets for sanitation and hygiene products and services will address the need for higher quality household sanitation facilities in rural areas; developing new initiatives beyond the traditional "Do-It-Yourself" model promoted through Community Led Total Sanitation. The activity will design and implement services, solutions and products that address "user needs" and preferences within their environments. Prior to approval, the activity will solicit customers' insights and reviews for prototypes while paying special attention to usability, practicality, and pricing. The activity will engage new and non-traditional partners to foster stable, resilient, and more self-reliant counties. Interventions will include capacity building of county governments and other stakeholders on the environmental impacts of poor community level sanitation and waste management. The Western Kenya Sanitation Activity will support the objectives of the 2022-2027 USAID Biodiversity Policy and Climate Strategy and contributes to the U.S. Global Water Strategy Strategic Objective One: Increase sustainable access and use of sanitation and the practice of key hygiene behaviors. Sustainable access to water and sanitation helps reduce conflict over resources, contributing to greater regional stability, a U.S. Foreign Policy priority. $1,200,000 will be used to meet the "safe latrines" earmark under this activity.. .

title.narrative: ENV: Sustainable management of Tsavo and Amboseli landscapes for resilient communities and ecosystems

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Through this activity, FY 2022 funds will scale-up landscape-level biodiversity conservation in areas that fall outside government protected areas in the Tsavo and Amboseli Ecosystems. Specifically, the activity will strengthen Kenyan institutions' capacity to foster a coordinated approach that enhances local stewardship, benefit sharing and the sustainable management of wildlife and biodiversity within the Tsavo and Amboseli Ecosystems. The activity will support improved governance of the landscapes, reduce threats and improve biodiversity conservation, increase partnerships for economic growth, and improve community and ecosystem resilience. In terms of climate adaptation, the activity will increase the community's ability to withstand environmental shocks and stressors through livelihood development and private sector engagement efforts; as well as conservancy / landscape management plans that set forth adaptation and preparedness measures in the region. .The activity will also focus on strengthening policies in natural capital; catalyzing private sector investments, and providing economic opportunities for women and youth. It will also promote research, monitoring, and learning through data analytics and knowledge management. The activity will also prioritize enhanced collaboration and partnerships with the private sector, conservancies, government, civil society, and other development partners working in the two landscapes. Ultimately, the activity will strengthen local institutions, expand wildlife space, improve livelihoods for communities, and establish partnerships with the private sector. The activity aligns with the U.S. government priorities through building local organizational capacities to drive local development. The activity also supports USAID's Biodiversity Policy, the U.S. National Strategy for Combating Wildlife Trafficking, Eliminate, Neutralize and Disrupt (END) Wildlife Trafficking Act and climate change. ....

title.narrative: ENV: Scaling Sustainability and Resilience of Community Conservancies in Northern Rangelands and Coastal Ecosystems of Kenya

description.narrative: (Kenya): USAID will utilize FY 2022 funds in the implementation of the Scaling Sustainability and Resilience of Community Conservancies in Northern Rangelands and Coastal Ecosystems of Kenya activity the goal of which is to contribute to building the resilience of communities, ecosystems and institutions in northern and coastal Kenya to reduce the vulnerability to environmental & climatic, economic and socio-political shocks. The activity will improve the ecological health of community-owned conservation areas; support holistic rangelands, forests, wildlife, water and marine resources management; and improve pastoral and tourism-based livelihoods. The activity will use digital ecological monitoring to collect, analyze and interpret data in real time to support decision-making and ecosystem-based adaptation approaches to protect endangered wildlife species and fragile habitats and enable them to adapt to and mitigate against climate risks. .The activity will enhance the well-being of people, livelihoods, and economy by securing community land rights--including women landowners in accordance with the Kenya's Community Land Act (2016)--; promote peaceful co-existence amongst different ethnic communities; and mitigate human-wildlife conflict. The goal is to expand economic opportunities for women and youth through increased entrepreneurial skills for nature-based enterprises in partnership with the private sector. To that end, the activity will promote private-sector led market-based approaches and investments in livestock, tourism, carbon, water, renewable energy within the conservancies. Finally, the activity will conduct institutional capacity strengthening of local conservation organizations including their governance, financial sustainability, and ability to engage in strategic partnerships with state and non-state actors to leverage private and public resources...... .. .. ..

title.narrative: HPN - Warehousing and Distribution of FP commodities

description.narrative: (Kenya): Support for family planning (FP) commodity security is a key priority for the Government of Kenya (GOK), USAID and other development partners. As part of its FP 2030 commitments, Kenya has pledged to increase domestic financing for Family Planning (FP) commodities to cover 100% of the requirements by 2026. To this end, the GOK signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with USAID, the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation to gradually increase domestic financing for FP commodities. In support of the MoU, USAID will utilize FY 2023 funds to support procurement, warehousing, and distribution of high quality contraceptives. .While procurement of the contraceptives will be facilitated by the Central Contraceptive Procurement (CCP) mechanism, this activity will focus on warehousing and distribution of the commodities to the last mile. Specifically, the activity will support clearance of all FP commodities through the port of entry, facilitate required quality assurance procedures, ensure good warehousing of the FP commodities in accordance with the national standards, facilitate distribution of FP commodities to the service delivery points, and report on the same. The implementing partner will receive guidance from the FP National Order Management Team (NOMT) in close collaboration with Kenya Medical Supplies Authority (KEMSA). These efforts will serve to build stable and capable local systems which in turn boosts U.S national security objectives and improves public opinions of the United States in Kenya, as well as asserting U.S. influence and leadership in global.
The project goal is to enhance accountability, efficiency, accessibility, and inclusivity in Kenyas electoral and democratic processes and improve citizens participation.

title.narrative: Kenya Sustainable Transformational and Accessible Water Interventions (STAWI)

description.narrative: The project aims to build resilience and expand economic opportunities through investments in water security in Kenyas arid and semi-arid lands..Working across nine target counties in northern and southeastern KenyaGarissa, Isiolo, Kitui, Makueni, Marsabit, Samburu, Taita Taveta, Turkana, and WajirSTAWI supports county governments to deliver basic drinking water services to 250,000 Kenyans and improve water service quality for 500,000 Kenyans, while also strengthening institutions and improving water resource management. Through technical assistance, a construction fund, and a local grants fund, STAWI takes an inclusive and integrated approach to address needs for drinking water, water for productive uses, and water resource management while building local capacity for collaboration, learning, and adaptation.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Academic Model Providing Access to Healthcare - People-centered, Leadership, Universal Access, Sustainability (AMPATH plus)

description.narrative: AMPATHplus aims to augment HIV care and control program and expand AMPATHpluss primary care activities. AMPATH PLUS will be a new phase in which the Moi University, Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital, and the Ministry of Health facilities work together to improve the health of our catchment area in Kenya. In this new phase, not only will we seek to find, link, treat, and retain all HIV-infected people within our catchment area, but we will also dramatically increase our primary care and chronic disease management services. AMPATH is poised to serve as a model of innovation, ultimately creating knowledge on the best practices that can be shared with other USAID programs, with the Government of Kenya and with healthcare systems throughout the world.

title.narrative: OEG- Assets-Based Financing for Smallholder Farmers Project II

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2017 funds, the Assets-Based Financing for Smallholder Farmers Project II (ABSFP II) activity will support 56,000 smallholder farmers in five counties to increase farm income and help decrease hunger and extreme poverty. ABSFP II will finance seed and fertilizer; train farmers to maximize seed germination and yields; use seedling nurseries to transplant new crops; teach effective drying techniques (to reduce the likelihood of rotting, pest infestation, and aflatoxin contamination); and advise on post-harvest management. The program will provide farmers with regular pricing information for larger markets, and train farmers on how to aggregate production. ABSFP II provides production materials to growers on loan, which the growers repay after harvest. ABSFP II ends on September 27, 2018.

title.narrative: OEGI - Kenya Resilient Arid Lands Partnership for Integrated Development (RAPID) WASH GDA

description.narrative: (Kenya): The purpose of the activity is to increase access to water and sanitation for people, increase access to water for livestock, and promote a healthy rangeland ecosystem. USAID is implementing this activity in line with the Government of Kenya's Ending Drought Emergency Common Program Framework (2014) which recognizes that sustainable management of rangelands, water, crops, and increasing contribution of livestock to the pastoral economy are critical to resilient livelihoods in arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs). The activity is implemented under a Global Development Alliance with the Swiss Development Corporation, private sector partners, and the Millennium Water Alliance, in five Northern Kenya ASAL counties (Marsabit, Garissa, Isiolo, Wajir, and Turkana)...USAID will use FY 2018 funds to support Kenya's county governments develop and implement county water sector policies; implement five private partnership business models; develop water, sanitation and hygiene sub-county capacity building plans; and facilitate implementation of the County Capacity Building Fund. The activity will also develop 53 new community water systems and rehabilitate existing facilities. USAID will use Foreign Assistance funds to support Community Led Total Sanitation that target communities that have become open defecation free. It will build the capacity of water and rangeland management committees; promote kitchen gardens; train households on key nutrients and food diversification strategies; and initiate nutrition education activities in schools...This activity promotes the utilization of U. S. government technologies and approaches in the water sector, such as the installation of borehole sensors to improve decision-making for better water service delivery and management. It will promote Kenya's journey to self reliance by strengthening water security in Kenya and increasing Kenya's ability to plan, finance and implement Kenya-led water stategies. ..

title.narrative: ENV- Climate Resilient Community Conservancies Activity

description.narrative: (Kenya): The Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Improvement by Community Conservancies in the Maasai Mara Region activity supports community driven sustainable biodiversity conservation and improves livelihoods in the Maasai Mara landscape in Kenya. The purpose of the activity is to: establish integrated and sustainable conservancy leadership and governance structures for community and privately managed conservancies; establish a mixed-model conservancy approach supporting improved landscape management, better wildlife security by securing critical wildlife migratory corridors, combating wildlife crime, and increasing economic opportunities and household income for landowners through establishment of a cattle enterprise; and strengthen Maasai Mara Wildlife Conservancies Association's (MMWCA) organizational systems and capacities to build effectiveness and accountability into constituent member conservancies, landowners, private sector, and development partners. FY 2018 funds will focus on upscaling and sustaining MMWCA's activities to achieve higher level results and long-term outcomes in the landscape. The activities will include: improving MMWCA's coordination capacity to support leadership and governance structures, assessing and strengthening MMWCA's organizational capacities as a membership body to coordinate community conservancies, and leveraging additional resources for sustainability. The program supports U.S. government security priorities, by countering illegal wildlife poaching and trafficking, as criminal activities have been known to help fund terrorist groups. This activity supports the U.S. National Strategy for Combating Wildlife Trafficking, the Eliminate, Neutralize, and Disrupt Wildlife Trafficking Act, and USAID's self-reliance agenda by helping Kenya's conservancies manage and plan for better conservancy governance systems, which in turn will help solve Kenya's development challenges in conservancy/wildlife sector.

title.narrative: ENV- Community Conservancy Policy Support and Implementation

description.narrative: (Kenya): Kenya's conservancies geographical areas are growing every year with private conservancies make up more than 3 million hectares. However, these conservancies face policy and institutional barriers to effectively carrying out their biodiversity conservation and sustainable-development mandates. The Community Conservancy Policy Support and Implementation activity seeks to address policy barriers inhibiting development of conservancies by promoting a supportive legal environment that encourages sustainable and beneficial conservation. This activity undertakes in-depth analyses of the range of policies and regulations that are necessary, applicable, and relevant for effective and sustainable conservancy operations based on secure land tenure. Then it develops an implementation strategy and action plan for all of the priority policies and regulations identified in the initial analysis. The focus has been on laws, policies, and regulations that pertain to biodiversity, wildlife, land, water, human rights, gender, law enforcement, and devolution within the context of the Community Conservancy model which is USAID/Kenya's flagship biodiversity conservation program. The Nature Conservancy, is the premiere organization in Kenya dedicated working in the area of conservancy policy to help Kenya build resilient human and natural communities that are better equipped to adapt to an uncertain future that includes drought, economic shocks, and political change. FY 2018 funding will support completion of the Community Land Act, 2016 Regulations; Implementation of the Regulations under the Wildlife Management and Conservation Act 2013; and Organizational Capacity Assessment of Kenya Wildlife Conservancy Association (KWCA) and systems strengthening. These interventions support U.S. priorities through inclusive and sustainable development, law enforcement, and ecotourism. This helps create an investment opportunity for U.S. businesses and a tourist destination for Americans

(Kenya): This mechanism will build on activities supported during Kenya's 2017 electoral process and address the political process, civic engagement and conflict mitigation emerging after the general election. Interventions may include defending civil society against closing space, strengthening capacity for civic engagement at national and county levels, greater inclusion and representation of youth, women, and marginalized groups, promotion of national dialogue that seeks solutions to root causes of conflict, strengthening conflict mitigation mechanisms at national and local levels, enhancing citizen access to government information and services, and strengthening elections and political processes and systems. A key focus will be to prepare Kenyans and Kenyan institutions to fundamentally address weaknesses experienced before, during, and after the 2017 general elections.

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The Health Communications and Marketing (HCM) activity.supports social behaviour change (SBC) interventions to increase demand and.uptake of health services. To shift from a dependance mindset to a.self-reliance mindset, behavior change is required to increase Kenyan.commitment. Additionally, local ownership and sustainability beyond donor.funding is a key focus of Kenya's journey to self-reliance. The community.to county level approach to designing and implementing SBC interventions.ensures local ownership and leadership, requiring intentional selection of.stakeholders who will be accountable for carrying activities forward. This.approach links health facilities and utilizes the existing cadre of community.health volunteers, which the Government of Kenya supports. HCM will support SBC.activities focused on increasing utilization of health services for HIV, family.planning, maternal, newborn and child health, and malaria through targeted.multi-channelled SBC strategies. In priority counties targeting the most.vulnerable and high priority populations, the focus of SBC activities will be.on increasing the uptake of postnatal care services, routine immunization,.prevention and treatment of diarrheal diseases through the community health.platform, increasing net utilization, early and appropriate health-seeking.behaviour, and prompt diagnosis and treatment for all people with fever. HCM.will provide technical assistance to the National Malaria Control Program and.the lake endemic counties to fulfill their advocacy, communication, and social.behavior change roles as defined in the Kenya Malaria Strategy. This activity.supports the promotion of a more healthy Kenya, which is a key American.economic, trading, and security partner in an often volatile East African region..By strengthening Kenya's health care system, USAID is helping to strengthen an.important regional ally..... .

title.narrative: HPN - SI CMLAP I Western Kenya

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The CMLAP I activity provides technical assistance in health information systems to county technical working groups; and supports the development and monitoring of performance improvement plans in Kakamega, Kisumu, Migori, Homabay, Turkana, Baringo, Samburu, and Siaya counties. Using FY 2019 funding, CMLAP I will work with the county reproductive health, maternal, neonatal, child, and adolescent (RMNCAH), TB/HIV and malaria managers to identify health outcome gaps, build the capacity of county health leadership to strengthen partner coordination structures, monitor health outcomes, and develop sound response measures to improve health outcomes. CMLAP I will build the capacity of Health Records and Information Officer's and other health workers on data analysis, visualization, and interpretation. Emphasis will be given to data quality improvement to ensure complete and accurate data in the District Health Information System, and review of maternal and perinatal death surveillance, and reporting response plans. The activity will organize bi-annual forums with USAID service delivery partners to review the quality of county RMNCAH scorecards. Quarterly review meetings with the Ministry of Health's department of family health will ensure alignment with national health information priorities. This activity will also work within malaria focus counties to strengthen monitoring and evaluation. CMLAP I is working with local governments' learning institutions to build their capacity to provide technical assistance withdata analytics for public health. This health systems' strengthening approach is a key element to ensure sustainability upon activity completion, which is vital to promoting the journey to self-reliance in the Kenya Health sector. It also supports the U.S. Administration's priority of promoting healthy, educated, and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development. .. .

title.narrative: HPN- Health Informatics Governance and Data Analytics (HIGDA)

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Health Informatics Governance and Data Analytics (HIGDA) provides support to the Ministry of Health's (MOH) Division of Health Information Systems and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Unit in the management of the National Integrated Health Management Information Systems. The activity provides technical assistance to improve the MOH's organizational, institutional, and leadership capabilities in information technology. HIGDA supports the MOH in developing and maintaining the Health Information Exchange infrastructure and proactively managing data access structures to protect patient privacy and ensure security of sensitive data. HIGDA, in collaboration with MOH Division of Health Information Systems and M&E, will support the National Malaria Control Program to strengthen leadership and governance for malaria health information systems through policy development and implementation of data quality protocols and standards. Utilizing a health systems strengthening approach for health information management is a key element to ensure sustainability upon project completion, which is vital to achieving the Kenya Integrated Country Strategy Goal 3, and U.S Department of State and USAID Joint Strategic Plan 2018-2022 objective 2.2 "Promote healthy, educated, and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets, and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives." Improving global public health supports the Administration priority of asserting U.S. leadership and influence..

(Kenya): .Afya Timiza focuses on advancing the journey to self-reliance in Turkana and Samburu counties by strengthening systems and building local capacity for family planning, reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, adolescent health, and nutrition. Using FY 2019 funds, Afya Timiza will prioritize leadership, management competencies, good governance, sustainable financing efforts, and accountability to enhance capacity and commitment for development programs. Domestic resource mobilization efforts will aim at securing at least 26 percent of the annual county budget for health. For greater social accountability between communities and county governments, the activity will use UNICEF's Citizen Voice and Action process. Data use within a collaborating, learning, and adapting approach will help to improve planning. To increase enrollment in the National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF), a livestock based financing option will be developed. Accreditation of health service providers under NHIF will be expanded and advocacy for NHIF provision for community health volunteers as an incentive framework will begin. The activity will support integrated supply chain systems, develop health worker retention strategies, and support county and sub-county health team mentorship activities for service quality improvement. Integration with HIV for client-centered services to reach hard to reach populations will be conducted through outreach services. Community and health facility activities will expand prevention and case management of diarrhea and pneumonia, improve nutrition, and expand key social behavior change interventions. The activity will collaborate and coordinate with USAID partners through the Partnership for Resilience and Economic Growth. In strengthening the health systems and institutions in these vast semi arid- counties, the activity aligns with U.S. security objectives and demonstrates strong U.S. leadership and influence in Kenya's health sector...

(Kenya): The Human Resources for Health Kenya (HRH) mechanism strengthens HRH management systems for better health outcomes. HRH contributes to the Journey to Self-Reliance by implementing the Afya Elimu Fund, a revolving fund that provides low interest tuition fees loans for students in medical training colleges. Beneficiaries then enter gainful employment and contribute towards better health outcomes. As loans get repaid, additional loans are extended to other students. Using FY 2019 funds, this activity builds the capacity of pre-service medical training institutions and Ministry of Health (MOH) in-service training programs. It supports the county HRH management units to ensure a well distributed workforce and strengthen the health worker information system for effective decision-making, and budgeting. Support for county HRH units includes advocacy for increased HRH resources, performance quality, and HRH strategies for attraction, deployment, and retention. Advocacy extends to the MOH and counties to adopt health workforce data systems, which are used to rationalize placement of health workers based on need. To support universal health coverage, community workforce development processes include training of community health extension workers and ensuring community services cadres are recognized so county governments are prepared to adopt and retain them. HRH additionally promotes county forums where workers' unions and county leadership can engage regularly to dialogue on issues and reduce labor disputes. Dialogues between county governments and unions also address the high absenteeism rates and staff turnover, which negatively impact HRH outcomes. Improved linkages with professional associations and continuous medical education institutions ensures health workers have the competence to provide quality health services, hence improving global public health, which supports the Administration's priority of asserting U.S. leadership and influence..

title.narrative: HPN - Afya Uzazi: FP/RMNCAH Nakuru and Baringo

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The Afya Uzazi project in Baringo and Nakuru counties by unlocking the potential of healthy, educated, and productive populations is driving inclusive and sustainable development to advance Kenya's journey to self-reliance. USAID investments strengthen health systems and build local capacity for family planning, reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health, nutrition, water, sanitation, and hygiene. Activities focus on building commitment and capacity at community, facility, sub-county, and county levels to respond to health needs of citizens, particularly poor and vulnerable groups. This activity builds the capacity of county and sub-county health managers on management, accountability, and governance to enhance ownership and reduce donor dependency. Counties are sensitized on domestic resource mobilization approaches to secure health funds. To support universal health coverage, the number of National Health Insurance Fund accredited facilities will be increased, and enrollment expanded to rural populations. This activity enhances the leadership role of the sub-county in health systems for integrated supply chain, enhancing the quality of the health information system, mentorship, and supportive supervision of health workers, and service quality improvement. Social behavior change through local organizations and community health volunteers prioritizes healthy timing and spacing of births, postnatal care for newborns, and broad social norm changes to prevent gender-based violence. Through a multi-sectoral approach, Afya Uzazi connects local health issues to larger development challenges through integrated population, health, and development activities. Strengthening county and local institutions' capacity ensures sustainable development and this activity protects America's values and leadership in disease prevention as indicated in Goal three of the State Department and USAID Joint Strategic Plan... .

title.narrative: HPN - HealthIT: Sustaining Use of District Health Information System II

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2022 funds, USAID will support the HealthIT activity, the goal of which is to provide technical support to the Ministry of Health (MoH) on the evolution and strengthening of sustainable health information systems (HIS) that are responsive to user needs, providing vital data for planning, decision making, and accountability within the health sector. ..More specifically, HealthIT will support the MoH in hosting HIS solutions in the new MoH data center in particular by working with the MoH to roll-out the Digital Health Platform (DHP), an integrated system that will support data management for all health program areas. The integrated DHP will provide critical data for tracking individual patient outcomes, program performance and prioritization of interventions. The activity will support the MoH and counties to generate quality Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH), nutrition, HIV/TB and malaria data for use in evidence-based decision making by all stakeholders; and provide real-time health commodities data through the Kenya Health Information System (KHIS) Health Commodities dashboard. Additionally, HealthIT will support the development of a digital platform for capturing household data that will inform net distribution to communities during the 2024 mass net campaign..Additionally, the activity will provide technical support in the maintenance of the Epidemic Preparedness and Response (EPR) dashboard that pulls data from the KHIS system to inform epidemic threshold setting and development of annual county EPR plans. Finally, the activity will use FY 2022 funds to provide technical support and oversight of TIBU-the national tuberculosis surveillance database. The activity will help integrate TIBU with other electronic medical record and surveillance systems including KHIS, DHP and Kenya Electronic Medical Records System both at national and service delivery points. This activity is also receiving HIV funds.

description.narrative: The Carter Center's overall goal is to strengthen Kenya's democratic institutions, support key Kenyan stakeholders in efforts towards genuine elections, and promote credible, peaceful general elections.The project objectives are to provide an impartial assessment of the long-term electoral process and to shape perceptions of key national, regional and international stakeholders regarding the quality, credibility and inclusivity of the Aug. 8, 2017 elections.Planned Outputs:.- In-depth assessment of the electoral environment (political, legal, and administrative aspects conducted in the pre-election, campaign and e-day periods).- Independent public statements released based on election mission assessments, highlighting key issues and potential challenges to the process.- Constructive political dialogue facilitated between key electoral actors.- Recommendations offered for electoral reform and improvements for future electoral processes.

title.narrative: Comprehensive Assistance, Support and Empowerment of OVC (CASE-OVC) in Central, Eastern and Part of Rift Valley

description.narrative: The Comprehensive Assistance, Support and Empowerment of Orphans and Vulnerable Children (CASE-OVC) programme is a five year, USAID-funded grant implemented by Christian Aid in Kenya. The programme aims to reach 170,000 orphans and vulnerable children, from 52,000 households, who are affected or infected by HIV and AIDS. The goal is to improve the well-being of the children by ensuring they can request and gain access to social services (health, nutrition, education, legal protection, psychosocial support and social protection). We are also working to improve their livelihood options to better care for themselves.

title.narrative: HPN - Afya Halisi: Reproductive Maternal Newborn Child Health (RMNCH) National County

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Afya Halisi supports the journey to self-reliance in Kisumu, Kakamega, Migori, and Kitui counties by strengthening county systems and building local capacity for sustainable health outcomes in family planning, reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, adolescent health, and nutrition. Using FY 2019 funds, this activity builds county leadership, management, and governance skills through partnering with local organizations to expand community health programs and enhance public participation in county planning. Domestic resource mobilization efforts build skills for budgeting, planning, and policy-making to secure health funds. To support universal health coverage, the number of National Health Insurance Fund accredited health facilities is being increased and enrollment expanded among rural populations. This activity enhances the leadership role of the sub-county in health systems strengthening for integrated supply chain systems, enhancing the quality of the health information system, mentorship, and supportive supervision of health workers and service quality improvement. Specifically, service quality improvements focus on the provision of integrated family planning services, emergency obstetric and newborn care, antenatal care, intrapartum, and postnatal care for mother and newborn, prevention and case management of diarrhea and pneumonia, routine immunization, and promotion of infant and young child feeding. Social behavior change through local organizations will prioritize healthy timing and spacing of births, postnatal care for newborns, and broad social norm changes to prevent gender-based violence. At the national level, Afya Halisi helps to institutionalize annual inter-governmental performance reviews. Through its guidance, USAID efforts support the Kenya Integrated Country Strategy Goal three, and the State Department and USAID Joint Strategic Plan 2018-2022 objective of demonstrating U.S. values and leadership in global health...

title.narrative: OEGI-Crops and Dairy Market Systems Development Activity

description.narrative: (Kenya): The Kenya Crops and Dairy Market Systems (KCDMS) activity will foster inclusive and sustainable agriculture-led growth by facilitating avenues for smallholder farmers, aggregators, processors, and other agricultural value chain actors to diversify into higher-value products and increase market access. KCDMS also promotes pathways to better nutrition through the production and consumption of nutrition-dense foods. Using FY 2021 funds, in alignment with the U.S. government priorities including climate change considerations, KCDMS will continue strengthening the capacity and commitment of county governments to invest in agriculture in order to enhance food security at the county and national levels. The activity will also enhance the voice of private sector and agribusiness associations to shape a favorable agribusiness enabling environment at county and national levels. The activity will co-create and implement food system interventions with lead firms that improve food security and market system resilience.With the KCDMS activity ending in September 2022, the activity has pivoted to ensure all interventions are Kenyan-owned and led. The activity will consolidate the gains made over the past three years through upgrading business management skills and improving agricultural product quality and quantity in order to meet end-market requirements. Focusing on strengthening market systems in the target value chains in partnership with the private sector, the activity is co-designing interventions that provide opportunities for youth and women-owned enterprises, a key objective under the Mission CDCS. KCDMS will continue assisting businesses for COVID-19 response and recovery. The activity will continue to promote trade opportunities along targeted value chains for regional and international markets. $2,000,000 of funding within this IM contributes to meeting the required "Micro, Small and Medium-sized earmark".. .

title.narrative: Agile and Harmonized Assistance to Devolved Institutions (AHADI)

description.narrative: With the adoption of the 2010 Constitution, Kenya set itself on a path toward devolutiona new system of governance that includes 47 county governments with governors and legislatures. The Agile Harmonized Assistance for Devolved Institutions (AHADI) is to support Kenyas vision of devolution. AHADI aims to promote governance systems that are transparent, accountable, effective in service delivery, and responsive to empowered citizens by working at national and county government levels. In partnership with Kenyan institutions, AHADI enhances capacity of the local and national government to implement devolution by piloting innovative tools, providing knowledge sharing mechanisms and building capacity to benefit both devolved and national-level institutions. Activities are led, planned and implemented with Kenyan leadership in government and civil society as well as in close coordination with other development partners. AHADI supports county governments and citizens to learn from each other and integrates citizen participation into training, policy development and research activities to provide a key link between citizens and government.

title.narrative: EDY - Tusome Early Grade Reading Program

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The new basic education activity will build on the success of the Tusome ("Let's Read" in Kiswahili) early grade reading program. It will expand interventions in English and Kiswahili for grades four to six throughout Kenya and help students in grades one to three reach higher levels of reading fluency through additional support. Using FY 2019 funds, activities may include teaching and learning materials development, technical assistance to Government of Kenya (GOK) officials, building the capacity of Kenyan publishing and printing companies, working with local youth organizations to promote a culture of reading, and a rigorous monitoring and evaluation platform to build the GOK capacity to assess student learning outcomes and use the data for decision and policy making. In support of Kenya's Journey to Self-Reliance, the new activity will build upon Tusome's strong foundation of host-country ownership, financing, and a long-term return on investment, as stated in the GOK's five-year Medium Term Plan. The new basic education activity will be co-designed with the GOK and other stakeholders to meet the priorities of Kenya's 2018-2022 National Education Sector Strategic Plan, the U.S. Global Strategy for Basic Education, and USAID's Education Policy to ensure USAID's investment in basic education leverages GOK financial and political commitment. USAID's demonstrated leadership and partnership with the GOK in developing foundational language and literacy skills through the full primary cycle in the Kenyan education system advances U.S. influence in Kenya. New activities will support the Joint Strategic Plan objective to "promote healthy, educated, and productive populations" by developing skills that enable academic success and eventual employment..

title.narrative: DGC- Civil Society Conflict Mitigation Program (SCORE)

description.narrative: (Kenya): The SCORE activity builds the capacity of civil society organizations (CSOs) to mitigate conflict and counter violent extremism in the six counties along Kenya's coast. SCORE assists these organizations to mobilize citizens, especially women and youth, for public participation at the local levels. In FY 2017, the SCORE activity will provide grants-under-contract to at least 14 local CSOs that are credible actors and agents for change in their communities. Sub-grants will be designed to address the drivers of conflict as well as the push and pull factors that lead to violent extremism in local communities. SCORE will also build the capacity of each grantee to enhance the sustainability of interventions through targeted organizational and technical capacity development based on needs identified in organizational capacity assessments. The SCORE activity includes a rapid response mechanism that will provide funds to address emerging, urgent conflicts in target counties.

(Kenya): The Afya Jijini activity strengthens health systems and improves family planning, reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health in Nairobi County. Major activities include support to voluntary family planning; postnatal care; promotion of healthy spacing of births; emergency obstetric and newborn care; antenatal care; postnatal care for mother and newborn; prevention and case management of diarrhea and pneumonia at facility and community levels; routine immunization; and maternal nutrition. The activity will train health facility and community health volunteers to increase technical capacity; strengthen health information and supply chain systems for essential medical commodities; and enhance monitoring and supervision systems. These core interventions are vital as Afya Jijini focuses on select informal settlements of Nairobi County with some of the greatest health needs. Utilizing a health systems strengthening approach is a key element to ensure sustainability upon activity completion, which is vital to achieving the Kenya Integrated Country Strategy Goal 3 and the U.S. Department of State and USAID Joint Strategic Plan 2018-2022 objective 2.2 "promote healthy, educated, and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets, and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives." Improving global public health supports the Administration's priority of asserting U.S. leadership and influence..

description.narrative: (Kenya): USAID is urging increased commitment from the Government of Kenya (GOK) to take on greater responsibility in addressing health issues benefitting Kenyans. In partnership with other development partners, USAID is leading an effort to secure a sliding scale financing agreement with the Ministry of Health (MOH) to realize increased GOK allocations for contraceptive resources, as donor resources decrease. Once the MOH approves this agreement and provides the first tranche of funding to the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority (KEMSA), USAID and other development partners will procure contraceptives based on the national MOH supply plan..KEMSA is a commercial parastatal whose functions include procurement, warehousing, and distribution of medications and medical supplies. Utilizing a Kenyan corporation for the procurement, warehousing, and distribution of medications and medical supplies is a key contribution to Kenya's journey to self-reliance. The project will procure, warehouse, and distribute contraceptives from the central warehouse to over 7,000 public health facilities in all 47 counties. In addition, KEMSA will support procurement, warehousing, and distribution of HIV commodities with funding from President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), as well as the warehousing and distribution of malaria commodities with funding from the President's Malaria Initiative (PMI). Funding will strengthen the GOKs health sector capacity to manage complex supply chain systems. This serves to build a more stable and capable MOH which in turn boosts U.S national security objectives and improves public opinions of the United States in Kenya, as well as asserting U.S. influence and leadership in global health...

description.narrative: (Kenya): .This activity supports the journey to self-reliance in Kilifi County by building commitment and capacity to strengthen health systems and ensure achievement of health goals in family planning, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health (RMNCAH), nutrition, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. It will build the leadership and management capacity of Kilifi County to finance and implement its health programs through prioritizing domestic resource mobilization, especially for the financing of RMNCAH services. This activity will enhance the capacity of county and sub-county teams to plan, coordinate, implement, monitor, and evaluate RMNCAH, nutrition, and WASH services. This approach will be anchored in co-creation and co-investment with the county and other stakeholders to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the health information systems, integrated supply chain systems, and human resources for health systems. Health workers contracted by USAID under the previous mechanism will be transitioned to the county payroll. To increase accountability for quality health services, this mechanism will use a co-creation approach to establish sub-county mentorship teams that conduct supportive supervision activities and build technical skills of health and community health workers. Sub-county teams will develop community-demand creation activities to increase utilization of health services and expand adolescent responsive services to address high teenage pregnancy rates within Kilifi County. By utilizing a health systems strengthening approach, the project ensures sustainability upon project completion, which is vital to achieving the Kenya Integrated Country Strategy Goal three, and U.S. Department of State and USAID Joint Strategic Plan 2018-2022 objective, which seeks to promote healthy, educated, and productive populations to drive inclusive and sustainable development..

Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: OEGI- KALRO: Integrated Agricultural Research and Development: Enhancing Food and Nutrition Security Through Increased Production and Agri-Business in Kenya

description.narrative: (Kenya): The purpose of Integrated Agricultural Research and Development activity is to undertake adaptive research to enhance growth and increase the competitiveness in the dairy, staples, and horticulture value chains. FY 2018 funds will be used to increase the capacity research officers within the Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) through advanced training. This includes integrated soil management, biotechnology development, and animal nutrition research activities. Other areas of research include drought resistant crop varieties, nutrition-dense leguminous plants, and high value fruit trees. Additionally, this activity will perform seed multiplication activities to provide planting materials to small-scale farmers, as well as research on emerging threats to farming, such as the Fall Armyworm, maize lethal necrosis, and east coast fever, among others. Partnering with KALRO, the leading agricultural and livestock research entity in Kenya, affords USAID significant synergy and leverages U.S. investments in terms of realizing agricultural innovations, knowledge, improving livelihoods, and the commercialization of Kenyan agriculture through increasing productivity and fostering value-chains. The activity supports the U.S. government's development agenda and Kenya's ability to implement solutions to solve its own development challenges by enhancing increased trade in biotechnology products, through equipping researchers with adequate skills to handle technical issues like biotechnology appropriately. The activity also supports the Government of Kenya's Big Four agenda through the Food Security and Nutrition Pillars.
The goal of the program is to address the challenges currently facing wildlife conservation in Kenya.

title.narrative: OEGI - Improving food security through strengthening and enhancing KEPHIS' regulatory capacity to certify crops and facilitate safe food (FOODSCAP)

description.narrative: (Kenya): The Agriculture Regulatory Capacity activity increases availability of quality seeds; mitigates against crop losses through plant health management strategies and diagnostics; and monitors food safety by promoting checks for food contaminants and supporting a pilot program to identify appropriate pesticide residue limits. The purpose of the activity is to improve food security by providing clean planting material, pest management solutions, and safe food by developing supportive seed production systems. The implementing partner is the Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Services, whose comparable advantage is its ability to provide science-based regulatory services through assuring quality of agricultural inputs and produce to promote food security and sustainable development in Kenya...USAID will invest FY 2018 funds to generate quality certified seeds for drought-tolerant crops; facilitate quick release of seed varieties; mitigate against crop losses due to plant health related causes; and monitor food safety. Where standards do not currently exist, the activity will work with the pesticide industry and other stakeholders to establish supervised field trials and coordinate regional field trials to develop maximum residue limit guidelines for locally produced crops. The drought tolerant crop varieties that will be released by KEPHIS will increase the options for farmers, especially in semi-arid areas of eastern Kenya. There is a specific focus on key "orphan crops" that are nutrient-dense and easily grown by vulnerable households. ..The activity promotes a Kenyan-led effort to prevent crop loss due to crop diseases and provides methodology to ensure food safety for the Kenya market as well as ex[port markets. The activity will foster opportunities for U.S. businesses economic interests through paving the way for a more transparent and professional seed system by addressing previously restrictive provisions to international trade in seeds....
