title.narrative: ENV- Enhancing Biodiversity Protection in the Amboseli-Tsavo Ecosystem through Expansion of Community Conservancies and Wildlife Security

description.narrative: (Kenya): The Community Conservancies Seed Grant activity will strengthen the governance capacity of nascent conservancies in the Amboseli-Tsavo landscapes in Kenya through targeted training, commodities, and technical assistance to ensure inclusive, transparent, and accountable conservancy governance systems that are necessary to combat poaching and conserve biodiversity. This activity is one in a complementary portfolio that supports several landscape/wildlife projects. The activity's implementing partner, Big Life Ltd., manages the logistics for hundreds of local Maasai rangers, more than 40 permanent outposts and tent-based field units, 13 vehicles, and aerial surveillance-protecting 2 million acres of wilderness in the Amboseli-Tsavo-Kilimanjaro ecosystem of East Africa. Big Life Ltd. and other implementing partners combine best practices and will hold collaboration, learning, and adaptation seminars to make any necessary course corrections. FY 2018 funds will support comprehensive implementation of the Amboseli Ecosystem Trust organizational capacity building plan. Support will promote innovative ideas for enhancing biodiversity conservation, improving the connectivity of biodiversity hotspots, and strengthening anti-poaching and anti-trafficking efforts in the three target landscapes. This activity is an example of U.S. leadership through balanced engagement and effectively strengthens the sustainability of USAID's efforts in the area of African wildlife and conservancy investments. The activity also addresses USAID's self-reliance agenda by helping .Kenya's conservancy stakeholders manage and plan for better conservancy .governance systems, which in turn will help Kenyan stakeholders solve the development .challenges in the conservancy/wildlife sector. ...

title.narrative: ENV - Enhancing Capacity for Low Emission and Climate Resilient Development in Kenya

description.narrative: (Kenya): .This activity supports Kenya's efforts to pursue long-term, transformative development and accelerate sustainable, climate-resilient economic growth while slowing the growth of greenhouse gas emissions. It implements the National Climate Change Action Plan in collaboration with the Ministries of Energy and Petroleum, Planning and Devolution, National Treasury, county governments, universities, and private sector. The activity supports Kenya's Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDC) development and submission. FY 2016 funds will implement priority actions including: 1) technical assessment to establish the resources to meet the GOK pledge to reduce emissions by 30% by 2030; 2) implementation of a national sustainable greenhouse gas inventory system; 3) policy reforms to catalyze private sector investments in reduced emissions; and 4) support the National Environment Trust Fund to promote the use of clean technology. ...

Objectives for Kenya: To support Kenya’s efforts to pursue long-term, transformative development and accelerate sustainable climate resilient economic growth, while slowing the growth of greenhouse gas emissions. • Strengthen capacity for low emission development in Kenya. Build national and county institutions’ capacity to better coordinate climate change activities and climate finances. Enhance decision making for increased resilience to climate change impacts. Promote climate smart technologies and business opportunities

Provide technical assistance and training to strengthen sub-national government functions, including development of budgets, local revenue raising, provision of local public services, community planning, participation, and implementation of laws, regulations, policies, and programs. Develop and/or strengthen associations of local governments and/or local government officials.

title.narrative: Conflict Early Warning, Mitigation and Peace Building

description.narrative: Reduce the threat or impact of violent conflict and promote peaceful resolution of differences, ensure conflict sensitivity so as not to exacerbate sources of violence and/or establish an inclusive framework for peace and reconciliation which addresses all key drivers and mitigators of conflict. This includes activities aimed specifically at atrocities prevention, as well as activities intended to transform relationships to decrease the likelihood of future violent conflict. Develop and support early warning and response mechanisms such as early warning models and response protocols; conflict analysis; monitoring mechanisms and peace structures at different levels; peace building communication systems; confidence-building measures; crisis-response planning and management skills at the local and national levels; and means for rapid and effective response in the event of crisis. Support quick-impact, outcome-based activities required to demonstrate the positive impact of a peace process, operation or other event, such as mobilizing small grants for communities and local/national governments; ensuring delivery of services (e.g., "ministry in a box"); bringing local and national government authorities closer to their constituencies (e.g., town hall meetings, consultations, production and dissemination of information); generating employment for potential spoilers; and managing expectations.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: OEGI-Increasing Smallholder Farmer Productivity and Profitability (ISPP) Project

description.narrative: (Kenya): The USAID Increasing Smallholder Farmer Productivity and Profitability activity supports a collaborative, multi-donor approach to increase smallholder agricultural productivity and profitability for food and nutrition security in six arid and semi-arid counties of Kenya. The purpose of the activity is to achieve inclusive and sustainable agriculture-led growth; strengthen resilience among people and systems; and improve nutrition indicators among the target population. The activity's target value chains are green grams, pigeon peas, sunflowers, beans, and sorghum. The implementing partner is the Food and Agriculture Organization. USAID will use FY 2018 funds to increase the knowledge and capacity of small-scale farmers in the management and use of water for supplementary crop irrigation, enabling them to graduate from subsistence to commercial agriculture. The activity will ensure that farmers consistently supply produce to markets by addressing produce fluctuation challenges, which are a major concern for market players. In addition, the activity will provide specialized training to smallholder farmers in agribusiness and marketing to enhance access to identified market opportunities. Participating smallholder farmers with children under two years of age will improve their complementary feeding and overall household nutrition.Given that frequent droughts are a major driver of humanitarian assistance needs, this activity provides substantial assistance to target counties. Through this activity, USAID asserts U.S. leadership and influence by strengthening and elevating USAID's core capabilities to achieve greater development outcomes and leverage development investments. In addition, this activity promotes Kenya's journey towards self-reliance by linking resilience and food security with humanitarian and stabilization efforts to reduce future dependence.

title.narrative: OEGI-Livestock Market Systems – Leader with Associates

description.narrative: (Kenya): The Livestock Market Systems (LMS) Leader with Associates (LWA) activity enables chronically vulnerable households and communities to pursue improved economic opportunities in the livestock market system. LMS LWA leads a coordinated effort with six Associate Sub-Awards to provide comprehensive assistance to vulnerable households and communities that often struggle to escape poverty due to complex risks and exposure to recurrent shocks and stresses. The LMS Leader collaborates with each of the six Associate Sub-Awards by serving as a support platform for USAID's resilience focus countries in the Horn of Africa, including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan and Democratic Republic of Congo. The LMS LWA will use FY 2021 funds to administer grants under the associate awards in Kenya. The grant facility is designed to stimulate and partner with private sector businesses to catalyze economic development and community level grants to strengthen resilience capacities. Additionally, LMS Leader will continue to be the management platform for the Associate Awards issued under the LWA, with the aim of providing cost effective and centralized support, including centralized finance, procurement; operations; human resources; communications; monitoring and evaluation; and Geographic Information System services. LMS Leader will promote Kenya's sustainability by partnering with and strengthening the Kenyan county governments, private sector and civil society actors in the arid lands via the grant facility. These efforts will improve local actors' capacity to lead and develop a more robust, sustainable livestock market system in Kenya. These efforts will reduce the need for humanitarian aid and improve the economic vitality of areas and groups, including women and youth, that are most vulnerable to shocks and threats.$500,000 of funding within this IM contributes to meeting the required "Micro, Small and Medium-sized earmark".

title.narrative: OEGI - Associate Award 1: Expanding and Diversifying Viable Economic Opportunities in Kenya

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The purpose of the Expanding and Diversifying Viable Economic Opportunities in Kenya activit is to advance towards an integrated and inclusive market system that will enable local communities access diversified nutritious foods and increased incomes, for them to be more resilient to shocks and stresses in five counties. .FY 2020 funds will be used to support technical assistance and meetings to establish and create sustainability measures of appropriate standards and protocols for safe operation of livestock markets during and post COVID-19; training of livestock market managers in livestock markets operations; and start-up grants for micro-enterprises in these markets across five counties. The funds will also be used to support training, supply equipment, and technical assistance for local institutions to address existing livestock market system constraints in the target counties. Local institutions include livestock and trade departments in the county governments; local cooperatives and saving and credit cooperatives; farmers associations; livestock market associations; and other emerging county-based business associations. Funds will be used to provide technical assistance for start-up businesses supported.Support will lead to stronger local development organizations (producer cooperatives, farmers associations, business associations) able to demand for services and accountability from the county government, a more vibrant and inclusive livestock sector devoid of cartels, increased incomes and wealth for pastoralists making them more self-reliant and, less reliance on foreign aid during periods of shocks (droughts, floods, insecurity) that frequently affect Northern Kenya counties. It is expected that with a stronger, private sector, the result will be a vibrant livestock market system that presents commercial opportunities for U.S. companies; and generates income for poor pastoralists and advances Kenya's Journey to Self-Reliance.... .

title.narrative: OEGI - Resilience Learning Activity (RLA) Associate Award#3

description.narrative: (Kenya): FY 2023 Feed the Future funding to the Resilience Learning Activity (RLA) will facilitate learning for adaptive management, knowledge management, and stronger communication to align with USAID/KEA goals and the Government of Kenya's (GOK) Ending Drought Emergencies (EDE) framework.RLA will strengthen county and community resilience measurement; facilitate learning for adaptive management; and improve knowledge management, learning and communication to mitigate the impacts of shocks. RLA will ensure that resilience principles and shock responsive approaches are incorporated in county government County Development Implementation Plans (CIDPs) and annual development plans. Specific sub-activities include: 1) country level resilience profile mapping; 2) indicator alignment between USAID and GOK reporting requirements; 3) social behavior change communication; 4) knowledge and investment fairs; and 5) facilitating humanitarian and development assistance partners to sequence, layer and integrate resilience interventions in the resilience focus zones. The project will continue to promote the integration of gender, youth and social inclusion in planning and implementation to build resilience and create efficiencies and transparency in public services and budgets. RLA will also support USAID's role in coordinating development partner and GOK resilience interventions by hosting coordination platforms in the north and southeastern ASAL counties. This will bring together USAID, USAID partners, and the Government of Kenya (GOK) at national and sub-national levels to coordinate limited resources, learn from best practices, and develop and implement mutually-reinforcing activities and improve delivery of services in the target counties. RLA is co-funded by the Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance, Bureau for Resilience and Food Security, USAID/Somalia, and USAID/KEA operating units.

title.narrative: OEGI- Kenya Integrated Water Sanitation and Hygiene (KIWASH)

description.narrative: (Kenya): The purpose of the Kenya Integrated Water Sanitation and Hygiene activity is to help increase access of clean water, improved sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) to more than one million Kenyans. The activity will assist water service providers (WSPs) to expand household connections and extend networks to unserved communities. In rural areas, the activity will work with county officials, WSPs, and private entrepreneurs to expand and improve operations; and improve management of existing community drinking water systems. It will work with the Kenyan Water Resource Users Association to improve catchment area protection and water access, and improve sanitation and multi-use services. To improve access to sanitation services and reduce open defecation, the activity will work with counties that make strong commitments to apply the community-led total sanitation approach and engage with private sector providers to make access to household latrines/toilets more affordable. The activity will work through public health clinics and local organizations already active in the agricultural and health/nutrition sectors (community savings groups and community care groups), prioritizing locations with high percentages of malnourished or stunted children. The activity will integrate with other related USAID activities to complement and realize synergies.This activity will help the Government of Kenya and counties along it's journey to self-reliance by developing strategic planning skills, enhancing capacity, and better prioritizing WASH needs. Capacity enhancement for local staff is a key element to ensure sustainability upon project completion, which is important to achieving the U.S. government Mission Objective of improved governance and basic service provision. Providing access to water and sanitation in Kenya helps reduce conflict over resources, thus contributing to greater regional stability, a U.S. Foreign Policy priority.

title.narrative: EDY- Kenya Youth Employment and Skills (K-YES) Program

description.narrative: (Kenya): The Kenya Youth Employment and Skills program (K-YES) aims to enhance employment opportunities for young high school dropouts through vocational skills training that lead to either wage or self-employment. Specific activities include: support to vocational training centers across nine counties, business skills training complemented with improved access to financial services, and opportunities for small agribusiness enterprise development along key value chains. In FY 2018, K-YES will provide 4,000 youth with technical and soft skills for wage and self-employment. To promote sustainability, K-YES brings county government and the local private sector together to form a compact, solidifying, local ownership over the process of connecting vocational training with local employment opportunities. This structure is geared towards a sustainable solution concerning the youth bulge in Kenya as it moves the country long it's self-reliance journey, where the K-YES beneficiaries will be part of Kenya's development solutions in the future. Furthermore, increased economic and employment opportunities for youth reduces their susceptibility for recruitment into violent and extremist groups and increases the supply of skilled labor for the private sector. K-YES activities that train youth to participate in Kenya's economic development are aligned with the Department of State and USAID Joint Strategic Plan's (JSP) objective to "promote healthy, educated, and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets, and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives."

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The NIWETU program works to reduce.violent extremism (VE) among at-risk individuals and communities in Kenya..NIWETU accomplishes this goal through building Kenyan national and local.government institutions responsible for countering violent extremism (CVE) and.through support to community organizations and leaders. NIWETU will strengthen Kenya's National Counter-Terrorism Center, the.Kenya School of Government, and the Ministry of the Interior to improve.research, training, and technical CVE capabilities. At the local level, NIWETU.works in counties at high risk of VE attacks and recruitment, including Nairobi.and four in Kenya's northeast, strengthening county government and civil.society responses to VE. NIWETU will continue to provide technical support to.counties in the development and implementation of CVE action plans (CAPs), in.line with Kenya's national CVE strategy. CAPs create an ongoing platform to.bring together government and community organizations to plan and strategize.against local violent extremist threats to peace and security. Funds will be used to help national and county level officials, as well as CSOs, to conduct research and identify potential problem conflict and VE areas. Through these interventions, the Mission is addressing the Agency's self-reliance goals by helping Kenya to systemically plan and implement effective Kenyan-led CVE programs that will continue after this activity finishes. This program.will directly contribute to the Mission's Integrated Country Strategy (ICS),.specifically objective 1.3: Enhance the capacity of Kenyan institutions to.prevent and respond to security threats and to contribute to regional peace and.security within a rule-of-law framework. It will support the Administration's.focus on U.S. national security, promoting sustainable efforts to counter VE,.resulting in a more stable Kenya that is better able to counter the threat of.VE domestically and in the region..

title.narrative: HPN - Afya UGAVI: Procurement and Supply Management Technical Assistance

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2023 funds, USAID/Kenya and East Africa (KEA) will fund the Afya Ugavi activity, the goal of which is to strengthen supply chain systems to improve both patient-level services and commodity security. The activity will prioritize interventions which further the primary health care objectives to maximize the impact of USAID investments, address data visibility and use, address health workforce capacity constraints, and support the delivery of improved whole person care that is more optimally integrated and coordinated. .Through an integrated approach, Afya Ugavi will focus on strengthening supply chain management systems at the national level and in 29 priority counties for the delivery and improved availability of quality health products and technologies. The activity will achieve these goals by strengthening the systems for commodity security and patient-centered pharmaceutical services, governance, and supply chain risk mitigation capacity. More specifically, this support will strengthen capacity for quantification, commodity logistics, and pharmaceutical services management; improve Ministry of health stewardship and oversight, stakeholder coordination, advocacy, and evidence generation for improved supply chain resource allocation; and strengthen monitoring and supervision systems, availability, and the use of logistics information for decision-making...Ultimately, the Afya Ugavi activity's mandate of strengthening health supply chains and pharmaceutical management systems are cornerstones for achieving USAID's global health efforts focused to end preventable child and maternal deaths; control the HIV/AIDS epidemic; control and eliminate malaria; combat infectious diseases; increase and sustain access to safe, voluntary, high-quality family planning and reproductive health services; and sustainably strengthen the health system. ..

title.narrative: Access to Clinical and Community Maternal, Neonatal, and Women's Health Services (ACCESS)

description.narrative: ACCESS worked with USAID missions, governments, nongovernmental organizations, local communities and partner agencies in developing countries to expand coverage, access and use of maternal and newborn health services and improve household health behaviors and practices. The Program promoted a continuum of care in womens health across the life cyclefocusing on women of reproductive age and extending, where opportunities existed, to younger and older women. ACCESS also improved health delivery by strengthening the facility, connecting the household to the facility, and mobilizing family and community members to make the links necessary to care for mothers and newborns. The Program improved access to knowledge of newborn health with the development and dissemination of tools and materials. This included the 2006 ACCESS-supported U.S. launch of the Lancet Maternal Survival Series, and production of a comprehensive learning resource package (Best Practices in Essential and Basic Emergency Maternal and Newborn Care). ACCESS also worked with in-service partners to train more than 1,000 providers in essential and basic emergency obstetric care and to improve the quality of obstetric services in hospitals and clinics. To improve care for low birth weight newborns, the Program supported host governments to implement and scale up facility-based Kangaroo Mother Care in hospitals and health centers in five countries.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

(Kenya): Kenya's devolved government includes 47 county governments consisting of executives and legislatures, as well as a national government. A new chamber of Parliament gives each county an elected Senator to represent its interests at the national level. Commissions that are responsible for implementing devolution will work with the National Assembly and the Senate on the legislative agenda. In FY 2014, USAID/Kenya will collaborate with the U.K. Department for International Development (DFID) on the Parliamentary Strengthening Program in Kenya to support entities responsible for oversight and facilitation of devolution and devolved functions. Tasks will include training and mentoring elected and appointed officials and staff of the Senate; providing technical assistance to both houses; and, facilitating involvement of citizens and civil society in the county and national legislative branches. Other tasks include technical assistance for institutions that prepare and draft legislation.

title.narrative: APHIA Plus Nairobi/Coast (AIDS, Population and Health Integrated Assistance)

description.narrative: (Kenya): APHIAplus Nairobi/Coast is an integrated bilateral project that covers both Nairobi and Coast Provinces, which host the largest cities in Kenya with unique characteristics and health needs. The project will run from 01/01/2011 to 12/31/2015. The total project life of funding is $55,000,000 from various sources, mainly PEPFAR, and to a lesser extent Global Health Child Survival account (GHCS). It supports Government of Kenya (GOK) structures at provincial, district, facility, and community levels in Nairobi and Coast Provinces. It supports integrated services including HIV, TB, Family Planning and Reproductive Health (FP/RH), Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health (MNCH), nutrition, water and sanitation interventions - while addressing the social determinants of health.The project addresses two main result areas: 1. Increased use of quality health services, products and information by: - Increased availability of an integrated package of quality, high-impact interventions at community and health facility levels - Increased demand for an integrated package of quality, high-impact interventions at community and health facility levels - Increased adoption of healthy behaviors - Increase program effectiveness through innovative approaches 2. Social determinants of health addressed to improve the well-being of targeted communities and populations to ensure - Improved food security and nutrition for marginalized, poor and underserved populations - Increased access to safe water, sanitation and improved hygiene - Expanded social mobilization for health.In FY14 MCH support will seek to improve prenatal clinic attendance, skilled attendance at birth and essential new born care with appropriate referrals for Prevention of Mother To Child Transmission (PMTCT). title.narrative: DGC- Supporting the Kenya Constitutional Implementation Process

description.narrative: (Kenya): .USAID continues to partner with the Government of Kenya in developing comprehensive laws and policies required under the 2010 Constitution. The technical assistance focuses on formulation and review of a whole new set of legal, regulatory and policy instruments in all relevant ENRM, land and governance sectors at the two levels of government. This assistance has resulted in a number of laws and policies being formulated and enacted. FY 2016 funds will support the judiciary on election related dispute resolution, and strengthen the Kenya Law Reform Commission (KLRC) and other agencies to undertake policy formulation, implementation, monitoring, and impact review processes to ensure that reforms in governance, land, environment, and climate change sectors are aligned to the Constitution. .

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Human Resources for Health (HRH) Capacity Bridge Project

description.narrative: (Kenya): The main goal of the Capacity Bridge mechanism is to strengthen Kenya's Human resources for Health (HRH) systems and capacity at national and county levels to build a sustainable health workforce. Using FY2015 funds, this activity will:1)Support development of devolved human resource management (HRM) policies and strengthen the HRM oversight function of the Ministry of Health at both national and county levels2)Support county HRH management systems, such as workforce forecasting, hiring, distribution, performance, and retention 3) Support USAID contracted health workers and their transition into county government payrolls.

title.narrative: OEG - Tegemeo Agricultural Policy Research and Analysis (TAPRA) II Program

description.narrative: (Kenya): Tegemeo Agricultural Policy Research and Analysis (TAPRA) II expands the analytical capabilities of Tegemeo Institute to do targeted impact analysis and agricultural assessments to monitor performance of the agricultural sector. This policy program contributes to the development of Kenya's agricultural sector by aligning Tegemeo's research activities and policy outreach with the Government of Kenya's Agricultural Sector Development Strategy and the Feed the Future (FTF) objectives and priorities. The TAPRA II project will also provide analytical capacity and information support to the county governments in the 22 FTF counties and to the national government as part of Kenya's efforts to address devolution policy challenges.

The project will provide support for Gender Based Violence (GBV) awareness and prevention activities, will establish a viable women's network, and will strengthen women's organizations and women leaders. Although this is a short project timeframe, the US Embassy views these activities as an important part of a USG conflict mitigation strategy in preparation for the 2012 elections. Women connected through a peace network will be equipped to rapidly mitigate violence. The local Peace Platforms will provide community members with a tool they can use to hold their local leaders accountable to the community, especially during the 2012 elections.

title.narrative: OEG - IR-Resilience and Economic Growth in Arid Lands-Improving Resilience (REGAL-IR)

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The goal of the REGAL-IR mechanism is to reduce hunger and poverty, increase resilience and social stability, and build a foundation for economic growth among pastoral communities in five counties of northern Kenya. Pastoralist communities, which predominantly inhabit these counties, are vulnerable to recurring and chronic droughts and have high poverty rates ranging between 49 to 94 percent...FY 2016 funding will support interventions in livelihoods and livestock value chain development, natural resource management, conflict mitigation, drought management, and improved nutrition in the targeted counties. These activities will contribute to achieving the mechanism's community resilience building goals, which include mitigation of, adaptation to, and recovery from shocks and stresses in a manner that reduces chronic vulnerability and facilitates inclusive growth. .....

description.narrative: This project includes the following two goals. Mitigate the impact of HIV/AIDS and decrease the risk of HIV transmission by facilitating and implementation of a comprehensive home based care package; and Provide holistic development and optimum care to children orphaned as a result of HIV and destitute grandparents under Nyumbani village concept.

title.narrative: Kenya Arid Lands Disaster Risk Reduction-WASH Program

description.narrative: The goal of the Kenya Arid Lands Disaster Risk Reduction WASH Program is to increase resilience to drought and flash floods while simultaneously increasing access to improved water supply and sanitation services and improving hygiene behaviors for poor and vulnerable populations in the arid counties of Turkana, Marsabit (including Moyale District), Garissa, Isiolo and Wajir.

USAID/Kenya's Financial Inclusion for Rural Microenterprises (FIRM) project is facilitating the expansion and innovation of financial service in agriculture, renewable/clean energy, water, and other sectors for the benefit of marginalized and excluded populations across Kenyan society. Since its launch in January 2011, the project has been promoting financing options for off-grid energy solutions. FIRM's scope has expanded to include work on accelerating financial closure of small renewable projects. Currently, FIRM is building a pipeline of bankable small renewable projects, which will subsequently be ranked for support (investment facilitation, pre-feasibility studies, project studies, transaction advisory services, and creating a fund to address the early stage development capital constraint). title.narrative: Kenya Medical Supplies Agency (KEMSA) Support Program in Kenya

description.narrative: This program will strengthen the Kenya Essential Medicines Supplies Agency (KEMSA) to play its rightful role in ensuring an effective supply chain that meets demand of the service sites throughout the country.

title.narrative: Kenya Feed the Future Innovation Engine (KFIE)

description.narrative: (Kenya): The Kenya Feed the Future Innovation Engine harnesses innovation for cutting-edge results through private sector-oriented strategies to generate significant measurable increases in household income and/or nutrition through efforts in selected agricultural value chains. Using FY 2015 funding, USAID will continue to support innovations that address limitations to agricultural production, improved soil fertility, improved agriculture productivity, improved market linkages for smallholder farmers, as well as supporting competitively selected innovations through a combination of catalytic grant funding and short-term technical assistance at various stages from proof of concept (Stage 1), through pilot roll-out (Stage 2), to transition to scale-up (Stage 3). This funding will be used for Stage 1 seed funding (up to $100,000) to incubate new ideas and support their transition to possible Stage 2 (up to $500,000) and Stage 3 (up to $1 million) activities.

title.narrative: AG-Resilience and Economic Growth in Arid Lands-Accelerated Growth (REGAL-AG)

description.narrative: (Kenya): This activity aims to increase resilience of economic growth in two counties as a model for the other seven counties in northern Kenya by: improving the policy enabling environment to increase economic growth; expanding end-market opportunities and catalyzing commercial investment; improving livestock productivity and promoting livestock value chain inclusiveness of women, youth, and local groups. A key focus involves facilitating behavior change in actors along the value chain from livestock keepers, middlemen, traders, transporters, and buyers. Using FY 2015 funding, activities will include the construction of four strategic commercial livestock markets, rehabilitation and upgrades of eight livestock feeder markets, and livestock sector business development grants.

title.narrative: OEG - KAVES (Kenya Agriculture Value Chains Program)

description.narrative: (Kenya): .The Kenya Agricultural Value Chain Enterprises mechanism seeks to reduce poverty among smallholder farmers and improve the nutrition status of women and children in 22 Feed the Future focus counties. ..FY 2016 funding will: 1) strengthen and promote smallholder production systems; 2) increase yields and reduce costs of production through transfer of low-cost technologies and practices; 3) source financial and technical assistance to reduce the costs of aggregation and marketing of food security crops, dairy, and other horticulture; 4) improve post harvest handling systems to reduce physical wastage and quality-related price erosion; 5) add value through processing crops and milk into manufactured products; 6) attract new private sector investments that increase demand for smallholder-based production systems; 7) support decentralized public sector capacity in regulation of commercial agribusiness based on smallholder producers; and 8) improve the land rights for smallholder farmers......

The Capacity Kenya project aims to strengthen health workforce policy and planning, build the knowledge and skills of health workers, and improve health worker productivity and retention.

The Leadership, Management and Sustainability (LMS) Program supports people and organizations around the world to strengthen the way they lead and manage their own programs to achieve widespread improvements in health. LMS/Kenyas programs work to strengthen leadership, management and governance for sustained health programs. Program activities focus on building leadership and management skills through training, mentoring and coaching. Allactivities are structured around the achievement of three intermediate results: 1) Improved management and leadership of the health sector and priority health programs on HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, family planning/ reproductive health, maternal and child health, and malaria; 2) Improved management and systems in health organizations and priority health programs; and 3) Increased sustainability and ability to manage change.
Drylands Livestock Development Program (DLDP) is a new program aimed at enhancing productivity and market cometitiveness of the livestock sector in pastoral areas of Kenya.

title.narrative: HED Partnership: A University Collaboration for transforming Higher Education in Africa at the University of Nairobi

description.narrative: University of Nairobi/Colorado State University: Centre for Sustainable Drylands: A University Collaboration for transforming Higher Education in Africa at the University of Nairobi - This partnership has established a Centre for Sustainable Dryland Ecosystems and Societies (CSDES) at the University of Nairobi (UoN) to address the challenges of sustaining Kenyas underdeveloped drylands.The objectives of the partnership are to:1) Improve the coordination of interdisciplinary education, research and outreach for drylands in Kenya; 2) Increase the capacity of students and faculty to address the problems of dryland ecosystems and societies; 3) Strengthen the research capacity and policy-relevance, and resource directions and innovations appropriate for Kenyan drylands; and 3) Increase participation in higher education by pastoralists, especially women, resulting in the development of more appropriate innovations for dryland systems.

title.narrative: Roads to a Healthy Future II (ROADS II) - Kenya

description.narrative: FHI 360s ROADS II project works with the National AIDS Control Council of Kenya to develop a standardized, high-quality, HIV prevention package that includes harmonized messages for mobile populations in Kenya. The project collaborates with partners in the APHIAplus programs to provide integrated solutions to health and development challenges in Kenya. ROADS II operates SafeTStop Resource Centres and interventions at four sites. At all its sites, ROADS II also addresses gender-based violence.

title.narrative: HED Partnership: Capacity Through Quality Teacher Preparation

description.narrative: Kenyatta University/Syracuse University: Capacity Through Quality Teacher Preparation - The partners are collaborating to strengthen the capacity of the teacher education faculty at Kenyatta University (KU) and build the program of education research. Activities include professional development programs, standardized teaching assessments and mentoring programs to prepare the teacher in training, support the novice teacher, and foster continual growth in the experienced teacher.

description.narrative: The Health Commodities and Services Management (HCSM) Program works to strengthen systems that deliver health care commodities and services focusing on key public health priorities especially HIV/AIDS, malaria, and reproductive health in Kenya.

(Kenya): MEASURE Evaluation (PIMA) improves monitoring & evaluation (M&E) capacity to collect, analyze and present data to inform planning and programming.Using FY2015 funds, this activity will:Review current National Reproductive Health (NRH) Strategy (2009-2015) and development of NRH strategy (2015-2018) -Maternal and neonatal death reviews/audits, dissemination and actions to prevent future occurrences-Data review and utilization of Reproductive, Maternal and Newborn Child Health scorecard and other appropriate tools. -Implementation of the revised national M&E plan and technical assistance to increase the capacity of the National Malaria Control Program M&E staff to ensure that data is used for decision making and program improvements-Strengthening of the malaria surveillance system at the county level by providing support for trainings to build capacity for surveillance, M&E, mentorship and reporting -Improvement of family planning unit's M&E capacity to collect, analyze and use data.

title.narrative: Kenya Primary Mathematics and Reading Program (PRIMR) Program

description.narrative: We are using innovative, data-based teaching and learning methods in reading and math to improve student outcomes in urban areas of Kenya. This method aims to teach the fundamental reading skills that are necessary for improving oral reading fluency and comprehension and the mathematics skills critical for improved number sense, computational fluency, and problem solving. In this three-year program funded by the US Agency for International Development, classroom data is being used to improve student achievement in reading and math, assessment data is determining the effectiveness of the reading and math interventions (with particular attention to gender equity), and the combined results are informing policy dialogue about the investments needed to improve outcomes for beginning learners.

The Partnership for an HIV-Free Generation/Kenya (HFG/K) is an innovative Public-Private Partnership that aims to reduce HIV incidence among Kenyan youth (ages 10-24 years) in half. HFG/K links the skills and assets of the private sector with PEPFAR and its implementing partners to make programs smarter and stronger. HIV-Free Generation/Kenya allows partners to maximize their investment dollars with matched funding, build meaningful business relationships, and work in an environment of technical innovation through partnerships with implementers, all while safeguard ing the youth of Kenya.

(Kenya): The Kenya Health Information System collects routine data at the health facility level via the District Health Information System (DHIS2) platform, which is the key data source for the National Malaria Control and Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (RMNCH) programs. Using FY2015 funds, this activity will:In select counties, strengthen the Health Information System and the collection of information at the health facility, sub-county and county levels. Improvements will be monitored through data quality audits. The investments will help improve the quality of data collected to inform decision-making for the National Malaria Control and RMNCH programs at all levels.

description.narrative: The USAID-funded Kenya Horticulture Development Project is a five-year 'Feed the Future' initiative funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and implemented by Fintrac, a leading US Agribusiness consulting company. USAID -KHCP is designed to achieve catalytic change leading to enhanced food security, increased incomes, and gender and youth equity in the horticultural sector. USAID-KHCP, in close collaboration with public and private sector organizations, employs a holistic approach to increasing competitiveness by delivering tailored assistance to entrepreneurial smallholder farmers with the aim to: 1) Enhance productivity and food security; 2) Increase value - addition; 3) Improving value - chain coordination, marketing, and trade promotion; 4) Improve business environment and institutional capacity.
